pr_title: fix(core): Fix supportedNodes for non-lazy loaded community packages (no-changelog)
pr_body:
## Summary
We had an inconsistency in how and when we prefixed `packageName` on nodes. This was causing `supportedNodes` referring to invalid node names.
This PR moves all `packageName` prefixing code to `LoadNodesAndCredentials`, which ensures that lazy-loading has no effect on node-names anywhere.

Extracted out of #9874.
[E2E Tests](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/actions/runs/12246693568)
[Workflow Tests](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/actions/runs/12246671270)

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts
* Fixes #8188
* Fixes #5501
* https://community.n8n.io/t/community-node-become-unrecognized-every-time-i-restart-n8n-container/52095
* https://community.n8n.io/t/community-node-is-no-longer-visible/46665


## Review / Merge checklist

- [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) <!--
   **Remember, the title automatically goes into the changelog.
   Use `(no-changelog)` otherwise.**
-->
- [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created.
- [x] Tests included. <!--
   A bug is not considered fixed, unless a test is added to prevent it from happening again.
   A feature is not complete without tests.
-->
- [ ] PR Labeled with `release/backport` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

issue_context.title: Reinstall missing packages with N8N_REINSTALL_MISSING_PACKAGES is messing up the node type and causing workflows to stop
issue_context.body:
First, thank you for building this great tool, I'm having a lot of fun! 😇 

**Describe the bug**
Community nodes are not being reinstalled after a redeployment of a new docker instance.

My setup is using a modified version of this template: https://github.com/railwayapp-templates/n8n

**To Reproduce**

My `Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
FROM n8nio/n8n:latest

ARG PGPASSWORD
ARG PGHOST
ARG PGPORT
ARG PGDATABASE
ARG PGUSER

ARG USERNAME
ARG PASSWORD

ENV DB_TYPE=postgresdb
ENV DB_POSTGRESDB_DATABASE=$PGDATABASE
ENV DB_POSTGRESDB_HOST=$PGHOST
ENV DB_POSTGRESDB_PORT=$PGPORT
ENV DB_POSTGRESDB_USER=$PGUSER
ENV DB_POSTGRESDB_PASSWORD=$PGPASSWORD

ENV N8N_BASIC_AUTH_ACTIVE=true
ENV N8N_BASIC_AUTH_USER=$USERNAME
ENV N8N_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD=$PASSWORD

# Reinstall missing packages: https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/troubleshooting/
ENV N8N_REINSTALL_MISSING_PACKAGES=true

CMD ["n8n", "start"]
```

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Set up an instance of Railway using this template: https://github.com/railwayapp-templates/n8n
2. Install a community node. In my case: `n8n-nodes-discord` from here: https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-discord
3. Add node to a workflow
4. Redeploy
5. Reload the browser
6. Workflow is now deactivated, and old node is not found, but I can create new nodes.
    1. `Workflow could not be activated: Node not found: n8n-nodes-discord.discord` 
8. _Sometimes uninstalling and reinstalling works, but it might cause more problems_
    1. After a couple of times this stops working and the node is not found even after reinstalling.

The package shows up as installed, but the workflows can't find the nodes.

![Screenshot 2023-02-17 at 10 52 57](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8380383/219545262-ff93952d-ce51-43b1-ba1e-26c649146dea.png)

**Expected behavior**
Missing packages should reinstall and workflows should be running and detecting the nodes after a docker instance redeploy. I expect the env variable `N8N_REINSTALL_MISSING_PACKAGES` would reinstall all packages. 

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Docker using `n8nio/n8n:latest`
- n8n Version: Version 0.216.0
- Database system: Postgres
- Operation mode: `own`

**Additional context**
Railway deploys do not allow me to persist the nodes directory mentioned here: https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/troubleshooting/

I will add more of my findings in this issue. Thank you! 😄

I've found another weird detail in the workflow JSON. The `type` of the node seems to be messed up after I've reinstalled the community node. I have no idea if this is due to the community node or due to the n8n core.

Here is my initial node `type` data compared to the new node:

```diff
    {
      ...
      "name": "Discord Send",
-      "type": "n8n-nodes-discord.discord",
+     "type": "n8n-nodes-discord.n8n-nodes-discord.n8n-nodes-discord.n8n-nodes-discord.n8n-nodes-discord.discord",
      "typeVersion": 1,
      ...
    },
``` 

So, this means, I'm able to add new nodes of the same package, but the old nodes don't work. It seems to me, that the `type` of the node is not consistent over multiple deploys.

Update: After another redeploy, the `type` change to `"type": "n8n-nodes-discord.n8n-nodes-discord.discord",`.

@Joffcom I've found a fix.

I had to go to the PostgreSQL table `installed_nodes` and replace the `type` values with the correct ones.

Messed up values:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8380383/224630292-bb8904e5-93d2-4120-898d-16074f8f2c4e.png)

Correct values:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8380383/224630663-f533f3a9-be55-4341-b16d-47128af24f30.png)


Then restart the container instance. And the old workflow works again.

I am uncertain if this is related to this issue: https://github.com/edbrdi/n8n-nodes-discord/issues/23
I don't think it is related to that issue but it could be, Normally editing the name of the node wouldn't matter. I still need to do a railway test to see if it is something related to that.

I have done some testing today and I was not able to reproduce this so I assume this has been fixed in an update at some point over the last few months although I was also unable to reproduce this previously.
